title: Fibre Products Base Change and Scheme Theoretic Fibres

items.title: The scheme fibre product represents compatible pairs of morphisms from every test scheme T; define its projections and Cartesian square.
items.statement: The scheme fibre product represents compatible pairs of morphisms from every test scheme T; define its projections and Cartesian square.

items.title: Two fibre products of the same diagram have a unique projection-compatible isomorphism.
items.statement: Two fibre products of the same diagram have a unique projection-compatible isomorphism.
items.strategy: Apply the universal property in both directions; both composites equal the identity by uniqueness.

items.title: Spec B times over Spec A Spec C is canonically Spec(B tensor_A C), as a product in all schemes.
items.statement: Spec B times over Spec A Spec C is canonically Spec(B tensor_A C), as a product in all schemes.
items.strategy: Use Hom(T,Spec R)=Hom(R,Gamma(T,O_T)) for arbitrary T, then the algebra coproduct; affine test schemes alone would be insufficient.

items.title: At a prime r of B tensor_A C, projections contract r to q in B and q-prime in C; the local maps are B_q to (B tensor_A C)_r and C_q-prime to that stalk and induce compatible residue-field embeddings.
items.statement: At a prime r of B tensor_A C, projections contract r to q in B and q-prime in C; the local maps are B_q to (B tensor_A C)_r and C_q-prime to that stalk and induce compatible residue-field embeddings.
items.strategy: Localize b maps to b tensor 1 and c maps to 1 tensor c; quotient by maximal ideals.

items.title: If P=X times_S Y exists, open V in X and W in Y mapping to an open U in S have product p-inverse(V) intersect q-inverse(W), an open subscheme of P. Also X times_S U=f-inverse(U).
items.statement: If P=X times_S Y exists, open V in X and W in Y mapping to an open U in S have product p-inverse(V) intersect q-inverse(W), an open subscheme of P. Also X times_S U=f-inverse(U).
items.strategy: Factor test maps uniquely through open subschemes; equality in U follows from its monomorphism into S. This lemma assumes existence only for P, not for all fibre products.

items.title: If Y is covered by open Y_i and products X times_S Y_i exist, their inverse images over overlaps glue to X times_S Y. The analogous assertion holds for a cover of S.
items.statement: If Y is covered by open Y_i and products X times_S Y_i exist, their inverse images over overlaps glue to X times_S Y. The analogous assertion holds for a cover of S.
items.strategy: Refine the available products by affine charts to apply the published affine gluing theorem. Open-restriction represents each overlap; uniqueness gives cocycles. For arbitrary T use preimages of the cover and glue its unique local maps. For a cover of S use both inverse images.

items.title: Every pair of scheme morphisms X to S and Y to S admits a fibre product, covered by Spec(B tensor_A C) for compatible affine charts.
items.statement: Every pair of scheme morphisms X to S and Y to S admits a fibre product, covered by Spec(B tensor_A C) for compatible affine charts.
items.strategy: First glue Y with X and S affine; reverse roles to allow arbitrary X over affine S; then glue over affine opens of S. Nonaffine overlaps are handled by open restriction, never assumed affine.

items.title: The category of S-schemes has binary products, terminal object S, and empty scheme as initial object; a product with the empty scheme is empty.
items.statement: The category of S-schemes has binary products, terminal object S, and empty scheme as initial object; a product with the empty scheme is empty.
items.strategy: The binary product is the fibre product; verify the other universal properties directly, including the zero ring spectrum.

items.title: There are natural symmetry, associativity and unit isomorphisms for products of S-schemes, compatible with every projection.
items.statement: There are natural symmetry, associativity and unit isomorphisms for products of S-schemes, compatible with every projection.
items.strategy: Describe maps from T as pairs or triples with common composite to S; every coherence identity follows from equal projections.

items.title: For S-prime to S, define X_S-prime=X times_S S-prime and f_S-prime on both structure morphisms and morphisms of S-schemes. A property is stable under base change if every such pullback retains it.
items.statement: For S-prime to S, define X_S-prime=X times_S S-prime and f_S-prime on both structure morphisms and morphisms of S-schemes. A property is stable under base change if every such pullback retains it.

items.title: Iterated base change along S-double-prime to S-prime to S is canonically base change along the composite, functorially in objects and morphisms.
items.statement: Iterated base change along S-double-prime to S-prime to S is canonically base change along the composite, functorially in objects and morphisms.
items.strategy: Identify test morphisms with the same compatible pair; identities and compositions agree after both projections.

items.title: For A-algebra C, base extension of A[t_i]/I is C[t_i]/I C[t_i]; base extension of S-inverse A is image(S)-inverse C, with no flatness assumption.
items.statement: For A-algebra C, base extension of A[t_i]/I is C[t_i]/I C[t_i]; base extension of S-inverse A is image(S)-inverse C, with no flatness assumption.
items.strategy: Verify the published module identifications are multiplicative; use polynomial universal maps and extended relations. Include arbitrary ideals, finite presentations as a special case, and zero ring outcomes.

items.title: Morphisms Spec K to X are pairs (x, embedding kappa(x) to K); in particular Spec kappa(x) to X is canonical and compatible with scheme morphisms.
items.statement: Morphisms Spec K to X are pairs (x, embedding kappa(x) to K); in particular Spec kappa(x) to X is canonical and compatible with scheme morphisms.

references.title: Stacks 26.13, paragraphs preceding 26.13.3 and its field-valued special case

items.strategy: Factor ring maps on an affine neighbourhood through localization and residue field; every neighbourhood of the image contains the whole one-point source. Prove independence of the chosen chart. Include the local-ring version: a local map O_X,x to A gives Spec A to X, because every open neighbourhood of the closed point of Spec A is the whole space. Include the equivalence of field representatives via a common extension, obtained from a prime of the nonzero field tensor product.

items.title: For any point s of S define X_s=X times_S Spec kappa(s), as a kappa(s)-scheme; allow nonclosed points, generic fibres and empty fibres.
items.statement: For any point s of S define X_s=X times_S Spec kappa(s), as a kappa(s)-scheme; allow nonclosed points, generic fibres and empty fibres.

items.title: For A to B and p in Spec A, the fibre is Spec(B tensor_A kappa(p))=Spec((A minus p)-inverse B / p(A minus p)-inverse B).
items.statement: For A to B and p in Spec A, the fibre is Spec(B tensor_A kappa(p))=Spec((A minus p)-inverse B / p(A minus p)-inverse B).
items.strategy: Use kappa(p)=A_p/pA_p, then localize and quotient, retaining all nilpotents.

items.title: The map X_s to X is a homeomorphism onto f-inverse(s), with kappa(x in X_s)=kappa(x in X); in an affine chart these are exactly primes q of B with q intersect A=p.
items.statement: The map X_s to X is a homeomorphism onto f-inverse(s), with kappa(x in X_s)=kappa(x in X); in an affine chart these are exactly primes q of B with q intersect A=p.
items.strategy: Apply prime correspondence to localization followed by quotient and check the basic-open topology; the residual fraction field is unchanged. Glue the identifications. There is no extra embedding choice for ordinary fibre points.

items.title: At x above s, O_(X_s),x is O_X,x / m_s O_X,x, equivalently O_X,x tensor over O_S,s kappa(s).
items.statement: At x above s, O_(X_s),x is O_X,x / m_s O_X,x, equivalently O_X,x tensor over O_S,s kappa(s).
items.strategy: Localize the fibre coordinate ring at the corresponding prime; use that elements outside p already become units in O_X,x.

items.title: Points of X times_S Y correspond to (x,y,s,r) with common image s and r a prime of kappa(x) tensor_kappa(s) kappa(y); the residue field is that of r.
items.statement: Points of X times_S Y correspond to (x,y,s,r) with common image s and r a prime of kappa(x) tensor_kappa(s) kappa(y); the residue field is that of r.
items.strategy: On compatible affine charts, localize both factors away from their contracted primes and quotient both prime ideals; primes contracting to the pair are precisely primes in the field tensor product. Check residue fields and inverse constructions, not merely a map from quadruples.

items.title: If s-prime maps to s, the fibre of X_S-prime over s-prime is canonically X_s times_kappa(s) Spec kappa(s-prime).
items.statement: If s-prime maps to s, the fibre of X_S-prime over s-prime is canonically X_s times_kappa(s) Spec kappa(s-prime).
items.strategy: Factor the residue-field point map through Spec kappa(s) and apply iterated base change.

items.title: For a k-scheme X and field extension K/k, affine charts of X_K have rings A tensor_k K, compatibly on overlaps.
items.statement: For a k-scheme X and field extension K/k, affine charts of X_K have rings A tensor_k K, compatibly on overlaps.
items.strategy: Apply the compatible affine product cover and localizations.

items.title: For a morphism f:X to S and s in S, choose an algebraic closure Omega of kappa(s) and define the geometric fibre X_bar-s=X_s times_kappa(s) Spec Omega.
items.statement: For a morphism f:X to S and s in S, choose an algebraic closure Omega of kappa(s) and define the geometric fibre X_bar-s=X_s times_kappa(s) Spec Omega.

items.title: Two choices of algebraic closure give isomorphic geometric fibres after transport of scalars by a chosen base-field isomorphism; no canonical choice is asserted.
items.statement: Two choices of algebraic closure give isomorphic geometric fibres after transport of scalars by a chosen base-field isomorphism; no canonical choice is asserted.
items.strategy: Assume Choice as in the published closure-isomorphism theorem; base change the chosen field isomorphism and its inverse.

items.title: Call a fibre geometrically reduced, integral, irreducible or connected when its base change to an algebraic closure has that property. Integral and irreducible require nonemptiness; the empty scheme is reduced and connected under the no-separation convention.
items.statement: Call a fibre geometrically reduced, integral, irreducible or connected when its base change to an algebraic closure has that property. Integral and irreducible require nonemptiness; the empty scheme is reduced and connected under the no-separation convention.

items.title: Open and closed immersions remain so under arbitrary base change; immersions (equivalently, locally closed immersions) do also. The pulled-back closed ideal is the image of the pulled-back ideal in the new structure sheaf.
items.statement: Open and closed immersions remain so under arbitrary base change; immersions (equivalently, locally closed immersions) do also. The pulled-back closed ideal is the image of the pulled-back ideal in the new structure sheaf.
items.strategy: Open case is inverse image. Closed case is C/IC on affine charts, glued; explicitly use the image ideal, since tensoring the original inclusion need not remain injective. Factor an immersion (equivalently, a locally closed immersion) as a closed immersion into an open subscheme.

items.title: Define the scheme-theoretic inverse image of a closed or locally closed subscheme Z of S under X to S as X times_S Z.
items.statement: Define the scheme-theoretic inverse image of a closed or locally closed subscheme Z of S under X to S as X times_S Z.

items.title: The intersection of finitely many closed subschemes of X is their fibre product over X and is cut out by the sum of their ideals; locally closed intersections follow by restriction.
items.statement: The intersection of finitely many closed subschemes of X is their fibre product over X and is cut out by the sum of their ideals; locally closed intersections follow by restriction.
items.strategy: For two ideals use (A/I) tensor_A (A/J)=A/(I+J), then glue and iterate.

items.title: Locally finite type and locally finite presentation morphisms remain so after arbitrary base change.
items.statement: Locally finite type and locally finite presentation morphisms remain so after arbitrary base change.
items.strategy: Choose witnessing affine source/target charts and affine charts of the new base mapping into them. Finitely many generators and, for presentation, finitely many relations survive coefficient extension.

items.title: Quasi-compactness is local on an affine cover of the target and is preserved by arbitrary base change.
items.statement: Quasi-compactness is local on an affine cover of the target and is preserved by arbitrary base change.
items.strategy: Prove target locality using finite principal refinements of any affine target open and finite affine covers of inverse images. Pull these covers back; the pulled-back affine charts are quasi-compact.

items.title: Finite type morphisms remain finite type under base change; products of two locally finite type (respectively finite type) k-schemes have the same finiteness property.
items.statement: Finite type morphisms remain finite type under base change; products of two locally finite type (respectively finite type) k-schemes have the same finiteness property.
items.strategy: For finite type combine local finite type with quasi-compactness. For products use tensor generators on affine charts; finite affine covers yield the global version.

items.title: A scheme morphism is affine if the inverse image of every affine open is affine.
items.statement: A scheme morphism is affine if the inverse image of every affine open is affine.

items.title: If finitely many global sections f_i generate the unit ideal and all nonvanishing opens X_f_i are affine, then X is affine.
items.statement: If finitely many global sections f_i generate the unit ideal and all nonvanishing opens X_f_i are affine, then X is affine.
items.strategy: The finite cover has affine pairwise intersections, principal in each chart. Localize its finite sheaf equalizer to prove Gamma(X,O)_f_i=Gamma(X_f_i,O). The canonical map to Spec Gamma is therefore an isomorphism on the corresponding principal covers, which cover the target because the f_i generate 1. This avoids relative Spec or a circular affine-morphism criterion.

items.title: A morphism is affine if the target has an affine open cover with affine inverse images.
items.statement: A morphism is affine if the target has an affine open cover with affine inverse images.
items.strategy: For arbitrary affine V, construct a finite principal cover whose members are principal in some original target chart. Prove the common-principal refinement inline: shrink to D_U(f) inside V, then D_V(g) inside that affine, which is principal in both. Pull back unit-generating functions and use the preceding affineness lemma.

items.title: Affine morphisms remain affine after arbitrary base change; compositions of affine morphisms and closed immersions are affine.
items.statement: Affine morphisms remain affine after arbitrary base change; compositions of affine morphisms and closed immersions are affine.
items.strategy: Check inverse images on new-base affine charts mapping into affine old-base charts, then apply target locality. Composition and closed immersions follow directly from the definition and quotient spectra.

items.title: Define Delta_X/S:X to X times_S X as the unique morphism with both projections identity.
items.statement: Define Delta_X/S:X to X times_S X as the unique morphism with both projections identity.

items.title: Under (X_S-prime times_S-prime X_S-prime) isomorphic to (X times_S X)_S-prime, the diagonal is the base change of Delta_X/S.
items.statement: Under (X_S-prime times_S-prime X_S-prime) isomorphic to (X times_S X)_S-prime, the diagonal is the base change of Delta_X/S.
items.strategy: Compare all projections from a test scheme; identify the Cartesian square of diagonals. No separatedness is used.

items.title: For an S-morphism f:X to Y, define Gamma_f=(id_X,f):X to X times_S Y.
items.statement: For an S-morphism f:X to Y, define Gamma_f=(id_X,f):X to X times_S Y.

items.title: The graph square with X to X times_S Y above Y to Y times_S Y is Cartesian, with right arrow (f composed with pr_X,pr_Y) and left arrow f.
items.statement: The graph square with X to X times_S Y above Y to Y times_S Y is Cartesian, with right arrow (f composed with pr_X,pr_Y) and left arrow f.
items.strategy: A test map into the pullback is uniquely determined by its X-coordinate: the second Y-coordinate is forced to be f of it. This does not assert graphs are closed without a hypothesis on the target.

items.title: For irreducible classical varieties over an algebraically closed k, the associated scheme of the classical product is the scheme product of the associated schemes; affine chart rings are the unreduced tensor products, which here are domains.
items.statement: For irreducible classical varieties over an algebraically closed k, the associated scheme of the classical product is the scheme product of the associated schemes; affine chart rings are the unreduced tensor products, which here are domains.

references.title: Vakil 10.1.3 and 10.4.E; local published affine product theorem

items.strategy: On classical affine charts use the published tensor-domain/product theorem; the isomorphisms glue by compatibility with projections. Thus reduction changes nothing in this setting. Do not generalize to arbitrary base fields or arbitrary reduced schemes.

items.title: Surjective morphisms of schemes remain surjective under arbitrary base change; in particular extension of the ground field does not turn a nonempty scheme into an empty scheme.
items.statement: Surjective morphisms of schemes remain surjective under arbitrary base change; in particular extension of the ground field does not turn a nonempty scheme into an empty scheme.
items.strategy: For a point of the new base choose a point above its image. The tensor product of its two residue fields over the base residue field is nonzero by vector-space bases; choose a maximal ideal (Choice) to obtain a point upstairs.

items.title: Open immersions, closed immersions and Spec(S-inverse A) to Spec A are monomorphisms of schemes; hence so are their composites.
items.statement: Open immersions, closed immersions and Spec(S-inverse A) to Spec A are monomorphisms of schemes; hence so are their composites.
items.strategy: Uniqueness of ring maps factoring a quotient or localization proves the affine cases for arbitrary test schemes; closed immersion locality gives the global statement. Composition is formal.

items.title: Ordinary reducedness, irreducibility, integrality and connectedness need not survive scalar extension: C tensor_R C splits, while F_p(u) tensor_F_p(u^p) F_p(u) contains nilpotents.
items.statement: Ordinary reducedness, irreducibility, integrality and connectedness need not survive scalar extension: C tensor_R C splits, while F_p(u) tensor_F_p(u^p) F_p(u) contains nilpotents.
items.strategy: Give the two ring identities directly in the remark; do not depend on B-page examples. Use C[z]/(z^2+1)=C times C and L[z]/(z^p-u^p)=L[epsilon]/(epsilon^p). The algebra identity is already published as ex-complex-tensor-square-over-the-reals, a B leaf which cannot be a dependency. Recompute the two-factor CRT identity inline from the cited A theorem; mint no new algebra claim. The new result is about scheme topology under base change.

items.title: A fibre retains its residue fields and nilpotents even though its underlying topology is the inverse-image topology; the underlying set of a general fibre product need not be a set product.
items.statement: A fibre retains its residue fields and nilpotents even though its underlying topology is the inverse-image topology; the underlying set of a general fibre product need not be a set product.

title: Fibre Products Base Change and Scheme Theoretic Fibres — Examples

items.title: For k[x,y,t]/(xy-t) over k[t], the fibre at a in k is Spec k[x,y]/(xy-a): at zero two reduced axes, at nonzero a a copy of G_m; the generic fibre has ring k(t)[x,x-inverse].
items.statement: For k[x,y,t]/(xy-t) over k[t], the fibre at a in k is Spec k[x,y]/(xy-a): at zero two reduced axes, at nonzero a a copy of G_m; the generic fibre has ring k(t)[x,x-inverse].

references.title: Specialization of the polynomial fibre computation in Vakil 10.3.1–2

items.strategy: Substitute t=a. For a nonzero solve y=a/x; at zero (xy)=(x) intersect (y). Use the same calculation over k(t).

items.title: The family k[x,t]/(x^2-t) has special fibre k[x]/(x^2) in every characteristic. Over Q the fibres at 1, 0, -1 and the generic point are respectively Q times Q, Q[epsilon]/epsilon^2, Q(i), Q(x) over Q(t).
items.statement: The family k[x,t]/(x^2-t) has special fibre k[x]/(x^2) in every characteristic. Over Q the fibres at 1, 0, -1 and the generic point are respectively Q times Q, Q[epsilon]/epsilon^2, Q(i), Q(x) over Q(t).
items.strategy: Substitute, factor and use the Chinese remainder theorem. At the generic point use t=x^2 and f(x)f(-x) to invert every nonzero polynomial; for characteristic 2 claim only the characteristic-independent zero-fibre statement.

items.title: The real affine conic Spec R[x,y]/(x^2+y^2+1) has no R-valued points, but its complex base change has point (i,0) and ring C[x,y]/(x^2+y^2+1).
items.statement: The real affine conic Spec R[x,y]/(x^2+y^2+1) has no R-valued points, but its complex base change has point (i,0) and ring C[x,y]/(x^2+y^2+1).
items.strategy: A sum of two real squares cannot be -1; evaluate after scalar extension at (i,0). Distinguish absence of R-valued points from the scheme being empty.

items.title: An integral R-scheme need not stay irreducible or connected over C: Spec C becomes Spec(C times C), also showing injectivity need not survive base change.
items.statement: An integral R-scheme need not stay irreducible or connected over C: Spec C becomes Spec(C times C), also showing injectivity need not survive base change.
items.strategy: Factor z^2+1 over C and use comaximal factors to identify C tensor_R C with C times C; identify the two primes and the projection to a one-point spectrum. The algebra identity is already published as ex-complex-tensor-square-over-the-reals, a B leaf which cannot be a dependency. Recompute the two-factor CRT identity inline from the cited A theorem; mint no new algebra claim. The new result is about scheme topology under base change.

items.title: A^1_k times_k A^1_k is A^2_k functorially; points over the pair of generic points are not unique, for instance primes (0) and (y-x) have the same contractions.
items.statement: A^1_k times_k A^1_k is A^2_k functorially; points over the pair of generic points are not unique, for instance primes (0) and (y-x) have the same contractions.
items.strategy: Use k[x] tensor_k k[y]=k[x,y] and identify Hom(T,-) with pairs of global sections; check contractions of the two displayed primes.

items.title: The fibre of Spec(A/I) to Spec A over p is Spec kappa(p) if I is contained in p, and empty otherwise.
items.statement: The fibre of Spec(A/I) to Spec A over p is Spec kappa(p) if I is contained in p, and empty otherwise.

references.title: Direct special case of Vakil 10.2.B and 10.3.2

items.strategy: The extended ideal in the field is either zero or the unit ideal.

items.title: For f:A^n_k to A^m_k given by polynomials f_j, its graph has ideal (y_j-f_j(x)) in k[x_1,...,x_n,y_1,...,y_m].
items.statement: For f:A^n_k to A^m_k given by polynomials f_j, its graph has ideal (y_j-f_j(x)) in k[x_1,...,x_n,y_1,...,y_m].
items.strategy: The coordinate map sends x_i to x_i and y_j to f_j(x); substitution identifies the quotient with k[x]. Obtain the same ideal by pulling back diagonal coordinate differences.

items.title: The zero fibres of x^2=t and x^3=t have the same one-point underlying space and residue field k, but are nonisomorphic schemes, of k-vector-space dimensions 2 and 3.
items.statement: The zero fibres of x^2=t and x^3=t have the same one-point underlying space and residue field k, but are nonisomorphic schemes, of k-vector-space dimensions 2 and 3.
items.strategy: Compare k[x]/(x^2) and k[x]/(x^3); their monomial bases distinguish rings as k-algebras. This adds a comparison rather than duplicating the worked quadratic fibre.

items.title: The open immersion Spec k[t,t-inverse] to Spec k[t] has empty fibre at t=0 because its fibre tensor ring is zero.
items.statement: The open immersion Spec k[t,t-inverse] to Spec k[t] has empty fibre at t=0 because its fibre tensor ring is zero.

references.title: Direct localization special case of Vakil 10.2.F and 10.3.2

items.strategy: In the tensor ring t is both invertible and zero, so 1=0. Compare with inverse image under the open immersion.

items.title: For k=F_p(v), L=k[u]/(u^p-v) is a field but L tensor_k L is L[epsilon]/(epsilon^p), so reducedness need not survive even algebraic scalar extension.
items.statement: For k=F_p(v), L=k[u]/(u^p-v) is a field but L tensor_k L is L[epsilon]/(epsilon^p), so reducedness need not survive even algebraic scalar extension.
items.strategy: The v-adic exponent shows v is not a pth power; apply the published p-power irreducibility lemma with n=1. In L set epsilon=z-u and use the characteristic-p binomial identity. The published integer-only Eisenstein criterion does not apply here.

items.title: For t maps to x^2, the self fibre product of A^1_k over A^1_k is Spec k[x,y]/(x^2-y^2): two distinct line components if char k is not 2, a doubled diagonal if char k=2.
items.statement: For t maps to x^2, the self fibre product of A^1_k over A^1_k is Spec k[x,y]/(x^2-y^2): two distinct line components if char k is not 2, a doubled diagonal if char k=2.
items.strategy: Factor (x-y)(x+y) when 2 is nonzero; otherwise x^2-y^2=(x-y)^2. Do not apply CRT to the intersecting line ideals.
